content.jointProblem: Can profiling-guided resource sizing and scheduling reduce GenovaMed’s Python/Snakemake pipeline toward below EUR 3 per sample and under 90 minutes per 24-sample batch while preserving clinically validated star-allele calls? The first experiment would profile representative batches and compare baseline execution with resource-allocation changes, testing whether scheduling methods demonstrated on other workloads transfer to this sequencing pipeline.

rationale.text: Popović has developed resource-aware scheduling methods that account for CPU, memory and storage differences, directly relevant to investigating inefficient cloud resource allocation.

sources.quote: The project developed theoretical foundations and practical algorithms for scheduling in distributed systems where nodes differ in CPU architecture, memory bandwidth, and storage speed.

rationale.text: His batch-scheduling research used workload distributions estimated from a bioinformatics cluster, providing relevant experience with heterogeneous computational workloads, though not evidence of star-allele pipeline optimisation.

sources.quote: parameters estimated from a three-month trace of a bioinformatics cluster at the University of Pécs.
We study the online scheduling problem in which jobs arrive over time with release dates, processing times that are unknown until completion

rationale.text: His workload-characterisation research supports an empirical approach to identifying resource demand and variability before selecting an optimisation policy.

sources.quote: Statistical properties analysed include inter-arrival time distributions, job size (CPU × memory × duration) distributions, diurnal and weekly periodicity, and user-level burstiness.

rationale.text: He has practical industry experience advising on VM placement and capacity planning, relevant to turning profiling results into deployment decisions.

sources.quote: advising on VM placement policy and capacity planning models.

constraints.text: Evaluate the existing Python/Snakemake workflow at its operational cadence of two weekday batches of 24 samples; treat the cost and runtime targets as hypotheses, not guaranteed outcomes.

sources.quote: Our bioinformatics pipeline takes a batch of 24 samples from raw sequencing reads to a final star-allele call in roughly four to six hours.
We run two batches a day on weekdays
We wrote the pipeline ourselves in Python using Snakemake
getting compute cost below 3 EUR per sample and ideally cutting total run time to under 90 minutes

constraints.text: Clinical accuracy must remain unchanged, and any production changes must fit the laboratory’s accredited quality-management and clinical-review processes.

sources.quote: without touching the clinical accuracy of the calls.
Our laboratory is accredited under ISO 15189 and every report is reviewed by a clinical pharmacist before it leaves the building.

constraints.text: Use of retained clinical samples must remain within their ethics approval; sharing operational traces and accessing genomic data require separately agreed permissions and safeguards.

sources.quote: a set of retained clinical samples held under ethics approval
willing to share anonymised traces for joint research

constraints.text: Scope implementation and validation around the company’s limited staff allocation and approximately EUR 8,000 annual discretionary R&D budget.

sources.quote: The two-person bioinformatics team and two senior molecular biologists can dedicate roughly two days per week each to a collaborative project
a small discretionary R&D budget of approximately 8,000 EUR per year.

constraints.text: If faculty infrastructure is used, schedule experiments within its off-peak access restriction rather than assuming continuously available capacity.

sources.quote: His group's OpenStack testbed (16 nodes) is available to partners during off-peak periods.

risks: Scheduling results from bioinformatics-cluster traces and other cloud workloads do not establish effectiveness for this short-read star-allele workflow. The first experiment must test that transfer on representative GenovaMed batches.
Alignment and allele calling are only suspected bottlenecks. Profiling may reveal serial algorithms, storage or data-transfer limits that resource scheduling cannot sufficiently improve.
The supplied material does not establish expertise in clinical star-allele validation or Snakemake implementation; company bioinformaticians and clinical staff must cover these responsibilities.
Faculty OpenStack results may not reproduce on the company’s cloud VMs or under its billing model. Current instance types, storage charges and interruption behaviour are unknown.
The researcher’s personal availability and project allocation are unknown, despite the stated availability of two supervised PhD students for collaborative work.
Permission to share sequencing data or operational traces is unconfirmed. An operational-trace anonymisation protocol does not by itself establish adequate protection for genomic data.
The cost and runtime targets may conflict or prove infeasible within the available budget, particularly if algorithmic changes or substantial clinical revalidation are needed.
questions: Can Popović confirm his availability, expected supervision effort and which students could participate in a scoped joint project?
Can GenovaMed provide the Snakemake DAG, software versions, representative batch logs, per-rule resource measurements and itemised cloud bills?
Which cloud provider, VM types, storage configuration and billing components underlie the EUR 9 per-sample baseline, and which costs must count toward the EUR 3 target?
Which representative and difficult CYP2D6/CYP2C19 cases, reference calls and acceptance criteria will be used to verify unchanged clinical performance, and who approves production changes?
What do the existing ethics approval and data-processing arrangements permit regarding researcher access, data export, faculty-testbed use and publication of anonymised traces?
Can the first experiment compare baseline and resource-tuned runs with fixed pipeline versions and inputs, measuring end-to-end runtime, full compute cost, resource utilisation and call concordance?
What interruption tolerance, recovery behaviour and turnaround guarantees apply if spot instances are tested?
What project deadline, procurement limits and allocation of the annual R&D budget are available, and is the 90-minute target measured from raw-read availability to final calls?
